William P. Gottlieb photographed trombonist Al Grey, who played with Count Basie and Duke Ellington. Gottlieb's famous jazz photographs began in the 1940s, and he later gave all his pictures to the public domain.

Women Cultivating Sugar Cane
This photograph from the National Archives shows African American women cultivating sugar cane by hand. Jack Delano took many pictures of farm work in the South and in Puerto Rico.
How would you cultivate a field of cane?
A 1980 U.S. Olympic Team Member in a Cowboy Hat
Warren K. Leffler photographed a member of the 1980 U.S. Olympic team wearing a cowboy hat at the White House. The team, back from Lake Placid, had won gold in hockey.
What would you wear to meet the president?
President Carter and Rosalynn Carter with an Olympic Athlete

Warren K. Leffler photographed President Jimmy Carter and First Lady Rosalynn Carter with a member of the 1980 U.S. Winter Olympic team. The team included the hockey players who beat the Soviets in the Miracle on Ice.
Why was the hockey game called a miracle?
Flight Deck of Space Shuttle Columbia
This NASA photograph shows the flight deck of the space shuttle Columbia, the first orbiter, which flew in 1981. Rows of switches and screens surround the commander and pilot seats.
How many switches can you count?
Jazz at Montreux
Romare Bearden made paper cutouts, collages of bright colors, of a jazz scene at Montreux in Switzerland in 1982. Bearden was a great American artist who made art about music.
How can torn paper show music?
Jackie Onassis in Court
Marilyn Church sketched Jacqueline Kennedy Onassis in court in 1982 in a case about a photographer who followed her. Courtroom artists draw because cameras are not allowed.
Why can't cameras go in a courtroom?
Salvation Army, Selma, Alabama
John Margolies photographed a Salvation Army building in Selma, Alabama, in 1982. Margolies photographed roadside architecture across America.
What can a building's sign tell you?
Selma Drive-In, Selma, Alabama
John Margolies photographed a drive-in movie theater in Selma, Alabama, in 1982. The big screen towers over rows of parking spots.
Why would you watch a movie from a car?
Astronaut Deke Slayton
Warren K. Leffler photographed astronaut Donald Deke Slayton, one of the Mercury Seven, in 1983. Slayton was grounded by a heart condition but flew in space in 1975.
How can a person who is grounded fly later?
Astronaut Gordon Cooper
Bernard Gotfryd photographed astronaut Gordon Cooper, one of the original Mercury Seven, in 1984. Cooper flew the last and longest Mercury mission in 1963.
What would you think about during a day in orbit?
Margaret Truman Launderette, Key West
John Margolies photographed a laundromat in Key West, Florida, called the Margaret Truman Launderette in 1985. The name is a joke on the president's daughter.
How do places get funny names?
Old Pro Golf Space Course, Ocean City, Maryland
John Margolies photographed a miniature golf course with a space theme, with a giant astronaut statue, in Ocean City, Maryland, in 1985. Roadside attractions copied the space age.
What would a space-themed golf course have?
Water Rats
Frank Meadow Sutcliffe photographed children bathing in the harbor at Whitby in northern England. He photographed life in the fishing town in the late 1800s, and the picture is called Water Rats.
Why would they be called water rats?
Joint Soviet-American Peace Quilt
This peace quilt from March 1986 was stitched by women in the United States and the Soviet Union. It carries the message For Peaceful Skies.
Why would quilts be a good way to send a message?
Sally Ride Accepts an Award
Bettye Lane photographed Sally Ride, the first American woman in space, accepting an award from Ms. Magazine in New York in 1988. Ride flew on the shuttle Challenger in 1983.
What would you tell the first woman in space?
Storm, Looking Northwest, Nixon, Nevada
Robert Dawson photographed a storm approaching across the desert near Nixon, Nevada, in 1989. He photographed the American West for a project called The Great Central Valley.
What does a storm look like coming over a desert?
Rosa Parks and Jibreel Khazan
Otis Hairston photographed Rosa Parks with Jibreel Khazan, who as Ezell Blair Jr. was one of the Greensboro Four, in 1990. Parks had refused to give up her bus seat in Montgomery, Alabama, in 1955.
What gives a person courage to say no?
The Greensboro Four, 30th Anniversary

Otis Hairston photographed the Greensboro Four at the 30th anniversary of their lunch counter sit-in on February 1, 1990. Four college students sat at a Woolworth's counter in 1960, starting sit-ins across the South.
What does sitting still do for a cause?
Rosa Parks at a Pathways to Freedom Event
Rosa Parks speaks at a Pathways to Freedom event in June 1990. The civil rights hero worked for justice her whole life.
What would you like to ask her?
SR-71 Full Motion Simulator
NASA's Dryden flight research center got a moving-base simulator in 1990 to train pilots for the SR-71 Blackbird. Simulators let pilots practice emergencies on the ground.
Why is a simulator safer than a real plane?
Gordon Parks
Nancy Lee Katz photographed Gordon Parks, the great photographer and filmmaker, in 1991. Parks was the first Black photographer for Life magazine and directed the film Shaft.
What would you ask a photographer who did so many things?
Grand Marshal Nat Gray Leading the Young Men Olympian Anniversary

Edward K. Newman photographed Grand Marshal Nat Gray leading a parade of the Young Men Olympian Benevolent Association in New Orleans in 1991. The social aid clubs march in colorful suits with brass bands.
What would a New Orleans parade sound like?
Grand Marshal Harold Dudley of the Zulu Social Aid and Pleasure Club
Edward K. Newman photographed Harold Dudley, grand marshal of the Zulu Social Aid and Pleasure Club, in New Orleans in 1992. The Zulu club leads parades during Mardi Gras.
What do you wear to lead a parade?
Earl Coleman Jr. at a Jazz Funeral
Edward K. Newman photographed Earl Coleman Jr. singing at a jazz funeral in New Orleans in 1992. Jazz funerals begin with slow hymns and end with lively music.
Why would a funeral have a band?
Astronaut Irwin Salutes the Flag at Hadley-Apennine

This photograph shows Apollo 15 astronaut James Irwin saluting the American flag at the Hadley-Apennine landing site on the Moon on August 2, 1971. The lunar module and the lunar rover are beside him.
How does a flag stand on the Moon with no wind?
Trombone Shorty and Eddie Boh Paris
Edward K. Newman photographed Troy Trombone Shorty Andrews and Eddie Boh Paris in New Orleans in 1994. Andrews was a child musician who became a star.
Why do kids start playing in brass bands?
South Pole Region of the Moon as Seen by Clementine
This mosaic of about 1,500 images from the Clementine spacecraft in 1996 shows the Moon's south pole. Dark craters at the pole may hold ice.
Why would ice on the Moon be important?
Hubble Deep Field

In December 1995 the Hubble Space Telescope stared at one tiny patch of dark sky for ten days, and the image released in 1996 revealed about 3,000 galaxies. It showed that the universe was far fuller than anyone had known.
How can a dark patch have thousands of galaxies?
Linear Aerospike SR-71 Experiment, First Flight
A NASA SR-71 Blackbird takes off in 1997 carrying a test engine called the Linear Aerospike Experiment on its back. The test was for a new kind of rocket engine.
Why put an engine on the back of a plane?
True Color of Jupiter's Great Red Spot
This 1997 image from the Galileo spacecraft shows the Great Red Spot of Jupiter in roughly true color. The spot is a storm bigger than Earth that has raged for centuries.
What kind of storm lasts hundreds of years?
Layers in Valles Marineris on Mars
Mars Global Surveyor photographed layers of rock in the walls of Valles Marineris, a canyon on Mars that is 4,000 km long. The layers record Mars's ancient history.
How do layers tell a planet's past?
Hubble Images Reveal Jupiter Auroras
In 1998 the Hubble Space Telescope photographed glowing auroras above Jupiter's poles. Jupiter's auroras are huge and bright.
What causes an aurora?
Neptune from Voyager 2
This picture of Neptune is made from the last whole planet images that Voyager 2 took in 1989 as it flew by. The bright blue planet has dark storms and white clouds.
What makes Neptune blue?
Eileen Collins
Astronaut Eileen M. Collins looks through the window of the shuttle Columbia in 1999. She was the first woman to command a shuttle mission.
What would you see out that window?
Marchers Carrying Flags in Selma
Peter Pettus photographed participants, some carrying American flags, marching in Selma, Alabama, in 1965. The photographs were published in 1999.
Why would marchers carry flags?
Freedom Train to Alabama
A poster for a Freedom Train to Alabama asks for contributions for Selma voting rights marchers. Peter Pettus photographed these signs in 1965.
How could you help from far away?
Wright Flyer Replica in a Wind Tunnel
NASA tested a replica of the Wright Flyer in the 40-by-80-foot wind tunnel at Ames in 1999. Engineers wanted to see how the plane that made the first powered flight really handled.
Why test an old plane in a wind tunnel?
Dasht-e Kavir Desert, Iran
A satellite photograph shows the Dasht-e Kavir desert in Iran, with white salt flats and ridges of sand. It is one of the driest places on Earth.
What makes the white patches?
F/A-18 with Weapons Ready for Mission
A U.S. Navy photographer photographed an F/A-18 fighter jet with weapons ready for a mission in December 2001. Ground crews prepared planes on carrier decks.
Why does a jet need a big crew on the ground?
Alluvial Fan, Taklimakan Desert, China
A satellite image from NASA shows a giant alluvial fan, a fan-shaped pile of sediment, in the Taklimakan Desert of Xinjiang, China. The branching channels look like a tree from above.
What shapes do rivers make from above?
NASA Mars Rover, Artist's Concept
An artist's concept from 2003 shows a Mars Exploration Rover on the red planet. The twin rovers Spirit and Opportunity landed in January 2004.
How would you drive a car on Mars?
Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter, Artist's Concept
An artist's concept shows the Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter, which reached Mars in 2006 and photographed the surface in great detail. Its camera can see objects the size of a dinner table.
How could a satellite see something so small?
Mars Science Laboratory at Sunset
An artist's concept from 2003 shows the Mars Science Laboratory, later named Curiosity, at sunset on Mars. Mars sunsets look blue.
Why would a Mars sunset look blue?
Puffer Fish Kissing the Camera
Brocken Inaglory photographed a spotted puffer fish, Arothron hispidus, bumping his camera lens in the sea off the Big Island of Hawaii in 2004. Puffers inflate themselves when frightened.
Why does a puffer fish blow itself up?
Cape Town, South Africa, Perspective View
This 2004 picture from NASA's Shuttle Radar Topography Mission and Landsat shows Cape Town and the Table Mountain peninsula in a 3D perspective. The mountain rises behind the harbor.
How can a satellite make a 3D view?
Martian Landmarks Dedicated to Apollo 1 Crew
NASA named hills on Mars after the crew of Apollo 1, who died in a fire on the launch pad in 1967. The Spirit rover took the pictures of the hills.
Why would someone name a hill after a person?
Kepler Supernova Remnant
The Chandra X-ray Observatory made this view of the Kepler supernova remnant, the glowing cloud left by a star that exploded in 1604. The colors show different energies of X-rays.
What would a star exploding look like?
Orbit Insertion by Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter
This artist's concept shows the Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter firing its engines to enter orbit around Mars in 2006. The probe slowed so Mars's gravity could catch it.
How do you slow down in space?
Titan Viewed by Cassini Radar
The Cassini spacecraft used radar to peer through the thick orange haze of Titan, Saturn's largest moon, in 2005. The radar revealed dunes, rivers and lakes of liquid methane.
What would a lake of methane be like?
The Sombrero Galaxy
The Hubble Space Telescope photographed the Sombrero galaxy in 2005. Its bright center and dark dust lane look like a hat.
Why is it named the Sombrero?
NGC 1275
This Hubble Space Telescope image from 2006 shows the galaxy NGC 1275 at the center of the Perseus cluster. Red threads of gas stretch around it.
What do you see in the red threads?
A Sea Squirt on Soft Coral
Nick Hobgood photographed a colorful sea squirt on a soft coral on a reef in 2006. Sea squirts are simple filter-feeding animals that look like jewels.
What might a sea squirt eat?
Hoodoos in Bryce Canyon
Jon Zander photographed hoodoos at sunset in Bryce Canyon National Park in Utah in 2006. Hoodoos are tall spires of rock, shaped by frost and rain over millions of years.
How does ice make tall rocks like this?
B-17G and B-52H in Flight
An Air Force photographer photographed a B-17G Flying Fortress from World War II flying beside a B-52H Stratofortress in 2006. The two bombers were built almost 70 years apart.
What has changed in airplanes over 70 years?
Chaos at the Heart of Orion
NASA's Spitzer and Hubble telescopes photographed the center of the Orion Nebula in 2006. Newborn stars and gas swirl in a cloud so bright you can see it in the winter sky.
How can you see a nebula without a telescope?
A Stellar Ripple: The Cartwheel Galaxy

A false-color composite of the Cartwheel galaxy from Spitzer, Hubble, Chandra and GALEX shows a giant ring where a smaller galaxy plunged through the center. Ripples spread out like a pebble in a pond.
How does a ring form in a galaxy?
The Mark of a Dying Star
NASA's Spitzer and ESA's Herschel telescopes photographed a dying star in the constellation Lyra, called the Ring Nebula, 2,300 light-years away. The gas shed by the star forms a glowing ring.
What happens to a star at the end of its life?
King Penguins, Falkland Islands
Ben Tubby photographed king penguins on the West Falkland Islands in 2007. King penguins are the second-largest penguins and have bright orange patches on their necks.
How do penguins stay warm?
Albino Green Turtle
David Monniaux photographed an albino green sea turtle, Chelonia mydas, a very rare white turtle, in 2007. Without pigment the turtle looks pale pink.
Why would a white turtle be rare?
Red-headed Finch
Hans Hillewaert photographed a male red-headed finch at Sossusvlei in the Namib desert in Namibia in 2007. The small bird has a bright red head against the dry landscape.
How do birds find water in a desert?
The Matterhorn
This picture of the Matterhorn was taken in 2007 from the train to the Gornergrat in Switzerland. The pyramid-shaped peak is one of the best-known mountains in the world.
Why does the Matterhorn have such a sharp peak?
Palau de les Arts Reina Sofía, Valencia
Diliff photographed the Palau de les Arts Reina Sofía, an opera house in Valencia, Spain, in 2007. The futuristic building was designed by Santiago Calatrava and looks like a giant helmet.
What does the building remind you of?
A Surfer at the Wave
Brocken Inaglory photographed a surfer riding a wave at Santa Cruz, California, in 2007. The surfer leans along the green wall of water.
How does a surfer stay balanced?
Fluorite Crystals
Giovanni Dall'Orto photographed fluorite crystals in the natural history museum in Milan, Italy, in 2007. Fluorite forms cubes and comes in purple, green and blue.
What colors do you see in crystals?
Gold Dust Day Geckos Fighting
Thierry Caro photographed two gold dust day geckos fighting on a banana tree in Reunion in 2007. These bright green geckos defend their territory.
Why would two geckos fight?
Basilica of the Sacred Heart, Brussels
Markus Koljonen photographed the Basilica of the Sacred Heart in Brussels, Belgium, in 2007. It is one of the largest Art Deco churches in the world.
What does Art Deco look like?
Nagaoka Festival Fireworks
This photograph shows fireworks at the Nagaoka Festival in Japan in 2007. The Nagaoka fireworks display is one of the biggest in the country, with huge chrysanthemum bursts.
How do fireworks make different colors?
Carpenter Ant Queen
Richard Bartz photographed a queen of the carpenter ant Camponotus herculeanus in extreme close-up in 2007. Her strong jaws and eyes show in fine detail.
What do the ant's jaws look like?
Buzz Aldrin on a Tour
NASA photographed Apollo 11 astronaut Buzz Aldrin in 2007 with a tour guide at the Dryden Flight Research Center. Aldrin, the second person to walk on the Moon, loved to talk about space.
What would you ask someone who has walked on the Moon?
SOFIA Infrared Observatory Support Team
Members of the SOFIA team gather in front of the Boeing 747 that carries a telescope. SOFIA flew above the clouds to study stars in infrared light.
Why would a telescope fly on a plane?
Man Orchid
Hans Hillewaert photographed the man orchid, Aceras anthropophora, in 2008. Each flower looks like a tiny hanging man with arms and legs.
What does each flower look like?
Ammonite Lamp Post at Dusk, Lyme Regis
Michael Maggs photographed a lamp post decorated with an ammonite fossil on the Marine Parade at Lyme Regis, Dorset, in 2008. Lyme Regis is known as the Jurassic Coast because of its fossils.
What fossils could you find on a beach?
Anse Takamaka, Mahé, Seychelles
Tobi 87 photographed Anse Takamaka, a beach on the island of Mahé in the Seychelles, in 2008. Granite boulders and palm trees frame the clear water.
What would you do on a beach like this?
Bridgewater Causeway and Bridge, Tasmania
This photograph shows the Bridgewater Causeway and Bridgewater Bridge in Tasmania, Australia, in 2008. The causeway crosses the Derwent River.
Why would a causeway be built across a river?
Air Force Fire Training
Air Force airmen train in front of a giant fire in 2008. Firefighters practice against real flames so that they know what to do in an emergency.
How do firefighters stay safe near flames?
Cabot Square, Canary Wharf, June 2008
Diliff made a panorama of Cabot Square in the Canary Wharf district of London in June 2008. Three of London's tallest towers rise behind the fountain.
How tall do skyscrapers look from the ground?
Korean Traditional Dancer at Yongsan Fall Festival
A traditional Korean female dancer smiles at the 2008 Yongsan Fall Festival in Seoul. She wears a hanbok, the Korean national dress.
What colors does a hanbok have?
Moonbeam, Brest 2008
Ludovic Péron photographed the sailing yacht Moonbeam, a classic design by William Fife built in 1903, at the Brest maritime festival in 2008. Its white sails fill the wind.
What would it be like to sail on a hundred-year-old yacht?
Ifugao Tribesman, Banaue, Philippines
Uwe Aranas photographed a man of the Ifugao people in Banaue, Philippines, in 2008. The Ifugao built the famous rice terraces up the mountains.
How would you grow rice on a mountainside?
Caracol Falls, Brazil
Tiago Fioreze photographed Caracol Falls near Canela, Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil, in 2008. The falls drop about 131 meters into a canyon.
How loud do you think the falls are?
Library of the Guimet Museum, Paris
Athoune made a panoramic view of the library of the Guimet museum in Paris in 2008. The round room is lined with books and has a gallery and a glass ceiling.
What would you read in a room like this?
Albert Memorial, London
Diliff photographed the Albert Memorial in Kensington Gardens, London, in May 2008. Queen Victoria had it built in memory of her husband, Prince Albert.
Why do people build memorials?
Kerron Clement, Olympic Gold Medalist
This photograph of Kerron Clement, a gold medalist in the 400-meter hurdles, was shown in an exhibit at the Annenberg Space for Photography in 2008. He ran for the United States.
How do you jump hurdles while running?
Test Director Monitors Move of a Test Stand
Emmett Given photographed Ernie Wright, test director, monitoring the move of a rocket test stand at NASA in 2008. Engineers moved huge structures carefully.
How would you move a building-size machine?
X-15 Veterans Reunite at Dryden
NASA's Tony Landis photographed veterans of the X-15 rocket plane program reunited at Dryden in 2008. The X-15 flew higher and faster than any airplane in the 1960s.
What would they talk about at a reunion?
Front View of the Lunar Electric Rover
Regan Geeseman photographed the front of NASA's Lunar Electric Rover in 2008, a pressurized moon vehicle with 12 wheels that rotate. Astronauts could live in it for days.
What would you do in a moon car?
NGC 454
The Hubble Space Telescope photographed NGC 454 in 2008, a pair of galaxies, a red elliptical and a blue irregular, that are pulling at each other. They are 100 million light-years away.
How do galaxies collide?
Celestial Sea of Stars
NASA's Spitzer Space Telescope captured a new view of a rich star-forming region in infrared in 2008. Glowing dust clouds hold thousands of stars.
What would a sea of stars look like?
